topic.title: Numeric Literals
topic.description: How to write numeric values in code

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore how to write numbers in code like a pro! You'll never look at numbers the same way again.

• How to write different types of numbers (whole, decimal, scientific)
• The secret codes for extra-large or tiny numbers
• Why some numbers need special letters (like F or D)

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're writing a recipe. Some ingredients need exact amounts (like 2 eggs), while others need precise measurements (like 1.5 cups of flour). Numeric literals are like these recipe measurements - but for code!

Numbers in code come in different flavors:
• **Whole numbers** (like 42) - perfect for counting
• **Decimal numbers** (like 3.14) - for precise measurements
• **Scientific notation** (like 1.5E3) - for really big or tiny numbers

Java treats numbers differently based on how you write them. For example:
- `5` is a whole number (int)
- `5.0` is a decimal number (double)
- `5F` is a float (smaller decimal)
- `5E2` is 500 in scientific notation

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Numeric Literals works:

steps.title: Basic Numbers
steps.description: Java automatically assigns types to numbers based on how you write them.
steps.code:
int apples = 5;          // Whole number
double pi = 3.14;       // Decimal number
float temperature = 98.6F; // Float needs 'F'

steps.title: Scientific Notation
steps.description: For very large or small numbers, use E notation. The E means 'times 10 to the power of'.

steps.title: Special Bases
steps.description: You can write numbers in different bases using prefixes.
steps.code:
int binary = 0B1111;  // 15 in binary
int octal = 07777;    // 4095 in octal
int hex = 0XFFFF;    // 65535 in hex

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ `5` is an int, `5.0` is a double - same value, different types
✓ Prefixes change number bases (0B for binary, 0X for hex)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Prefer double over float for better precision
Use scientific notation for very large/small numbers
donts: Don't forget the F for float (3.14 is double, not float)
Don't put underscores at start/end (45_ is wrong)
Don't use commas in numbers (1,000 is invalid)
sections.protip: When in doubt, use `double` for decimals - it's the most precise and flexible option!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Numeric Literals used in real apps?

examples.how: Use scientific notation for physics calculations (like 9.8E0 for gravity)
Use underscores in large numbers (1_000_000 for one million)

problem.description:
Write a program that calculates the area of a circle with radius 5.3. Use the correct numeric literals for:
1. The radius value
2. The π constant (use 3.14159)
3. The final result
hints: Use double for all values for precision
problem.explanation: We used `double` for all values to maintain precision. The radius (5.3) is already a double by default. The calculation gives us the precise area of the circle.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Numbers in code can be written in many ways - choose the right one for your needs
📌 `double` is your best friend for decimal numbers - it's precise and flexible
📌 Practice writing numbers in different formats (scientific, different bases)
📌 You're now ready to handle any numeric value in your programs!
